pr.title: Note every other state a pull request's row could show, and spell the holds out in an open drawer
pr.head: 66cbe48e16ef1b59c3fdb06f2e6b98c0dcf45ed0

summary: Projector's Claude Code mod draws a panel above the prompt with one line for each pull request the session fixes or reviews. Each line shows the pull request's number, one state word, the title, a few notes after the title, and an age. The state is the most urgent thing that applies, taken in a fixed order: conflict, failing, changes, threads, reviewing, clean, then draft or ready.

Before this change the notes named only the holds that the state had not already named. A hold is something that keeps the pull request from merging: a conflict, failing checks, a change request, or open review threads. The two labels a review sets, reviewing and clean, never showed as notes. So a signed-off pull request whose checks failed read failing, and nothing on its line showed that it still carried clean.

Now the notes name every other state that applies, in the state's order and each in its own color: failing, changes, and threads in short, then the reviewing and clean labels, then approved. A conflict always takes the state, so no note names it. While a pull request's drawer is open, its line spells the holds out as checks failing, changes requested, and the threads' count, such as 2 threads, and also names the hold that is already the state. The 2* count that used to end every line is gone, and each file in a drawer counts its threads the same way, as 2 threads or 1 thread.

cards.html:
• The first Projector review read head 8f359a0 and found it clean, with one suggestion: add a test row that has a hold and a reviewing label. Head 423fd9b adds that row, and removing the reviewing note from notesOf now turns the notes test red.

groups.title: Which notes a row shows
groups.kicker: The rule that picks a row's notes, and the open-drawer wording
intro: All of the change's logic is in hooks/register.tsx. HOLDS is the table of holds, most urgent first, and rowState picks the line's state word from it, then from the review labels. notesOf builds the notes after the title, and now takes whether the row's drawer is open.

Each hold now carries a phrase, a function that gives its full wording, in place of the old note. failing, changes, and threads have one, and the threads' phrase counts them with threadCount, which the drawer's file lines use too. conflict has no phrase, because it always wins the state, so it never becomes a note. The review labels move into a table, REVIEW_LABELS, that both rowState and notesOf read, so the two agree on the labels' order and colors.

checks.text: A note's color comes from the same HOLDS or REVIEW_LABELS entry that colors the state word, so a red or yellow note always matches the color that hold would get as the state. The collapsed line, which shows only numbers in statusColor, is unchanged.

files.note: notesOf now lists every hold and review label that applies, except the one that is the row's state, and spells the holds out while the drawer is open. Open threads are a hold note like the others, and the drawer's file lines count threads with threadCount.

checks.text: A closed row leaves out the hold that is its state, and an open row keeps it in its full wording. The isOpen || status !== shown test is the whole difference between the two.

A review label becomes a note only when a hold, or reviewing, took the state, because otherwise reviewLabel makes that label the state. So a running review over an earlier clean reads reviewing with a clean note.
threadCount gives both the open row's threads phrase and each drawer file's count, so the two always agree on 1 thread and 2 threads.

A loading row stays muted with no notes. Its placeholder from loadingOf in hooks/github.ts has no labels, no review decision, no threads, and no checks, so notesOf returns nothing for it. Checked by reading both functions.

groups.title: Tests and documentation
groups.kicker: The panel test that pins the rule, and the user guide's description of it
intro: The rewritten panel test reads the notes of six rows with every drawer closed, then opens three drawers and reads them again. It compares whole note lists, each part with its color, so a missing note, a repeated state, or the wrong open-drawer wording turns it red. Two new fixtures cover a signed-off pull request whose checks fail, p21, and a failing pull request under a running review, p22. The drawer tests now expect each file's count as 2 threads or 1 thread.

docs/plugins.md is the user guide for the panel. Its paragraph on notes now describes the new rule and the open-drawer wording, its drawer section describes the new file counts, and its example panel shows a row with a drawer open.

files.note: Replaces the old notes test with one that reads each row's notes by title, closed and open, and updates the drawer tests for the new notes and the spelled-out thread counts.

checks.text: The new row turns the test red when the reviewing note goes. Removing that label from the notes in notesOf at 423fd9b left 233 tests passing and failed this one on the Failing change a review is reading row. Checked by making that change, running claude plugin test, and restoring the file.
The helper takes the Text after a title as that row's notes, unless it is empty or looks like an age such as 5m, in which case the row has no notes.

files.note: Describes which notes a row shows, the open-drawer wording, that no note names conflict, and the drawer's spelled-out thread counts.

checks.text: The paragraph matches notesOf: the order, the colors, the open-drawer phrases, and the rule that no note names conflict. The example's lines still end in one column. Checked by reading both against the head.
